item.title: Paraguay on Watch for Downgrade at Fitch After Bank Collapse
item.description: Fitch Ratings placed Paraguay’s credit rating on watch for a potential downgrade on Wednesday, citing risks to the nation’s finances and economy from a banking crisis that toppled President Santiago Peña and rattled investors.

item.title: Nasdaq 100 Rallies as CoreWeave Quells AI Fears, Draws Buyers In
item.description: US technology stocks rallied Wednesday, with the technology-heavy Nasdaq 100 index nearly erasing losses since the US midterm election, as renewed excitement over the artificial intelligence trade lured dip buyers in.

item.title: Lula Unveils Plan to Curb Spending Growth in Bid to Calm Fiscal Worries
item.description: Brazil’s government unveiled a package of measures meant to shore up public finances and ease investor concerns about rising public debt, as President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva aims to alleviate fiscal fears that have roiled markets since his election victory.

item.title: Why Nordstrom Decided to Go Private
item.description: Nordstrom Co-CEO Pete Nordstrom, says that there is "a lot of headroom" in the firm's Rack concept and that he and his brother, Co-CEO Erik Nordstrom, wanted more influence over some of the company's decisions in explaining why they took Nordstrom private in 2025. He speaks with Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Funds Warn Brazil $126 Billion Stock Market Rout Isn’t Over
item.description: The rout in Brazilian assets sparked by Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s re-election shows little sign of abating, with some of the nation’s biggest money managers saying a downturn that has already wiped out months of gains could get even worse.
